newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH FUEL INDUSTRY EXPECTS EXCISE TAX RISE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH FUEL INDUSTRY EXPECTS EXCISE TAX RISE.

text.p: The Polish finance ministry may raise the excise tax on fuel in Poland by at least three groszes per litre in the next few days, fuel industry sources told Reuters on Tuesday.
"The rise is to be between three and five groszes per litre," one source, who asked not to be named, said. "It is to be announced on Tuesday or Wednesday," another source said.
The finance ministry's press office declined to comment.
The excise tax on imported fuel is now 876 zlotys per tonne of 94-octane leaded petrol, 791 zlotys per tonne of unleaded petrol and 440 zlotys per tonne of diesel.
A rise of between three and five groszes per litre would entail a rise of between 30 and 50 zlotys per tonne, or three to 11 percent, depending on the kind of fuel.
The sources said that the ministry decided to raise the tax only after the country's biggest fuel refinery Petrochemia Plock agreed not to raise its prices despite the tax increase.
Plock's spokeswoman Romana Kuffel did not confirm or deny this information.

The head of Poland's liquid fuel chamber Andrzej Szczesniak said an excise tax rise could boost prices of imported fuel but not necessarily by the same amount as distributors could lower their margins, now at 9-15 groszes per litre.
